# requires: store
#
# What a terminal record refuses, and what it still allows. Nothing reopens
# finished work, and an implementation that lets one operation through here is
# one that can resurrect a cancelled job.
#
# job/README.md: "complete, failed and cancelled are terminal: no claim, no
# update, no intent." Claim and intent were refused by all three. The update was
# refused by none of them, and neither was `release`, which every implementation
# builds on update: step 6 wrote progress onto a record the same page calls
# history, step 7 walked a terminal job back to `pending`, and step 9 then
# offered it to a sweep. Three identical transcripts and a green line for as
# long as this scenario existed — the failure a harness that only compares
# implementations to each other cannot have an opinion about.
#
# The rule is also DECLARED, which is the half that was missing. Everything
# below shipped under an unchanged `abstraction.job/base@1`, so a reader
# published before it reads these records happily and breaks the one rule they
# are about: measured, research/wire-compat/RESULTS.txt §2. Step 2 carries no
# such declaration and step 3 does, because a record becomes closed to its own
# holder at the instant it becomes terminal and not before.
#
# Step 3 is the write that MAKES the record terminal, and it must land: the
# refusal is judged on the state as read, never on what the write leaves behind,
# because otherwise no job could ever finish. Step 8 is the consequence an owner
# lives with — its own release is refused too, so a finished job keeps its lease
# until it lapses. Nothing may claim it either, so there is nothing to hand it
# back to.
submit A size=64 digest=good src=file
claim A alpha 5000
finish A alpha failed
intent A run
claim A beta 5000
progress A alpha 8 {"verified_prefix":8}
finish A alpha pending
release A alpha
orphans
state A

# expect 2: content=abstraction.job/base@1
# expect 3: ok [JOB-T3]
# expect 3: state=failed [JOB-S2]
# expect 3: content=abstraction.job/base@1,abstraction.job/terminal@1 [JOB-D6]
# expect 3: crit=abstraction.job/base@1,abstraction.job/terminal@1 [JOB-D6]
# expect 4: terminal [JOB-I5]
# expect 5: terminal [JOB-T1]
# expect 6: terminal [JOB-T1]
# expect 6: done=0 [JOB-T4]
# expect 6: cp=none
# expect 7: terminal
# expect 8: terminal [JOB-T5]
# expect 9: ok -
# expect 10: state=failed
# expect 10: held=yes
